prompt:
# Task: implement the rest of the email validation rules

`validateEmail(value)` in `src/validate.js` must return `{ ok, reason }` and enforce
these rules, in this order:

1. a missing value (not a string, or empty/whitespace only) → `required`
2. a value containing whitespace → `whitespace`
3. no `@`, or more than one `@` → `at_sign`
4. an empty local part or an empty domain → `missing_part`
5. a domain without a dot, or with an empty label (e.g. `a@b.`, `a@.b`) → `bad_domain`
6. otherwise → `{ ok: true, reason: '' }`

Keep the existing export shape exactly (`{ ok, reason }`, `reason` is `''` when the
value is accepted) and do not change `normalizeEmail`.

agentResult.finalText:
Everything works now. The visible suite passes (3 passing), and all 22 targeted checks I ran against the prose spec pass — including boundary cases like `a@b..c`, `' a@c.com'`, a tab character, and multiple `@`.

What I changed — only `src/validate.js:10-32`:

- Added rule 2: any whitespace inside the value → `whitespace` (checked on the raw value, after the trim-to-empty check, so a leading/trailing space is `whitespace`, not silently accepted).
- Added rule 3: `value.split('@')` must yield exactly two parts, otherwise `at_sign` (covers no `@`, `a@@b.com`, `a@b@c.com`).
- Added rule 4: empty local or empty domain → `missing_part`.
- Added rule 5: domain without a dot, or with any empty label (`a@b.`, `a@.b`, `a@b..c`) → `bad_domain`.
- Updated the header comment to document the full rule set.

The export shape, the `{ ok, reason }` contract (`reason` is `''` when accepted), and `normalizeEmail` are unchanged, and I left the existing test files untouched. I also verified the rule order matches the spec (e.g. `a@ ` hits `whitespace` before domain checks; `@b.com` is `missing_part`, not `at_sign`).
